incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment, acting through the Companies Register online portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company (companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz incorporation application), resulting in a certificate of incorporation issued under section 13 of the Companies Act 1993
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. New Zealand law prescribes no minimum paid-up capital for a limited liability company, no blocked escrow account, and no capital bank guarantee before incorporation. The board may issue shares for such consideration as the directors determine in accordance with the Companies Act 1993, and capital maintenance rules apply after issue.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF NZ_LTD, COMPANY NUMBER TO BE INSERTED, ADOPTED ON THE DATE TO BE INSERTED, AT THE REGISTERED OFFICE. IT IS HEREBY RESOLVED, in accordance with the Companies Act 1993 and the Constitution of the Company, as follows: 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: That the allotment of ordinary shares described in the share register be approved and ratified. The subscribers shall subscribe for and take up the number of ordinary shares set out in the application, credited as fully paid upon receipt of the subscription moneys. The directors are authorised to allot shares, issue share certificates, update the share register, and complete any return required by the Companies Office. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: That the establishment of one or more bank accounts with a bank to be selected by the directors is authorised. The directors, acting jointly or severally, are authorised to execute account mandates, payment service agreements, trade finance documents, indemnities, and standing instructions. All cheques, wire transfers, payment orders, and letters of credit shall be signed by any two authorised signatories, being the Managing Director, the Finance Director, and such additional person as the board designates. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: That the registered office of the Company is established at the address shown on the Companies Register, New Zealand. The registered office shall be open to the public during ordinary business hours. The directors are authorised to notify the Registrar of Companies and to change the registered office when required. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: That the persons named in the minutes are appointed as Managing Director, Finance Director, and Company Secretary. Each officer shall exercise the powers and perform the duties set out in the Constitution, the Companies Act 1993, and any board delegation. The Company Secretary shall maintain the statutory registers and comply with all filing obligations. 5. GENERAL AUTHORITY: That the directors and officers are authorised to execute all agreements, instruments, customs declarations, tax registrations, and regulatory documents necessary to carry on the business of wholesale remarketing of used construction excavators, and to open bank accounts, engage professional advisers, and incur ordinary expenses. These resolutions continue until revoked by the board. THIS BEING ALL BUSINESS, THE MEETING ADJOURNED.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name availability check and governance document preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Companies Register online portal (companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary name and governance design check with the New Zealand Companies Office. Access the Companies Register online name search tool and verify that the proposed company name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing company, foreign company, or reserved name. Ensure that the name ends with Limited or Ltd unless an exemption applies, and that any restricted word is supported by written consent from the responsible ministry. Prepare the optional constitution, fix the share structure, appoint the first directors, obtain signed consents to act as director and shareholder, and establish the New Zealand registered office. The subscribers may execute the incorporation documents electronically under the Electronic Transactions Act 2002, but each subscriber must verify identity for the Companies Office.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and alternative names
Subscriber consent forms and director consent forms
Share allocation schedule with class, quantity and nominal value
New Zealand registered office and postal address
Director and shareholder identification details and dates of birth
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or queried, select a different name or obtain the required approval from the relevant ministry; the application can be amended and resubmitted before payment is made.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Lodge incorporation application with the Registrar of Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Companies Register online portal via RealMe
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the Companies Register portal using a RealMe account and complete the online Application for Registration of a Company. Enter the registered office, postal address, director details, shareholder details, share classes, and any restrictions or special rights. Attach or adopt the constitution either as a bundled document or as the Companies Act 1993 default constitution. Each director and subscriber must consent in the prescribed manner; digital consent may be entered in the portal or uploaded as a signed consent form. Review the data summary carefully, pay the official incorporation fee through the secure payment gateway, and transmit the application electronically to the Registrar of Companies. The Registrar will assign a company number and issue a certificate of incorporation once the validation is complete and all statutory particulars are accepted.
required_dossiers: Adopted constitution in PDF or plain text
Consents of all directors and shareholders
Payment receipt for official filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is suspended or queried, correct the validation warnings, respond to the Companies Office within the stated deadline, and resubmit; if the issue cannot be resolved online, provide a written affidavit or clarifying statement to the Registrar of Companies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain certificate of incorporation and execute first board governance actions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office and the duly appointed first board of directors of NZ_LTD
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, download and retain the certificate of incorporation issued by the New Zealand Companies Office. Verify the company number, date, and name, and arrange for the certificate to be held in the statutory minute book. Ratify the allotment of shares to the subscribers, record the allotment in the share register, issue share certificates or electronic holding statements, and file any return of allotment with the Companies Office if required. Convene the first board meeting and pass the first board resolution adopting the registered office, approving the bank mandate, and appointing the Managing Director, Finance Director, and Company Secretary. Open the registers of directors, shareholders, and charges, and record the beneficial ownership information in accordance with the Companies Office rules on director and shareholder disclosure.
required_dossiers: Share register and share certificates or electronic holding statements
Registers of directors, shareholders, and charges
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains an error, use the Companies Office correction process; if the allotment return is queried, file an amended return and provide the board resolution and shareholder consent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete tax, customs, and overseas investment registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department, New Zealand Customs Service, and the Overseas Investment Office where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete post-incorporation tax and customs registration. Verify that Inland Revenue has issued or associated the company IRD number with the incorporation record; update the company postal and bank details in myIR. Register for GST if the value of taxable supplies in any 12-month period exceeds NZD 60,000 or if voluntary registration is preferred; register as an employer if employees are engaged. For cross-border trade in used construction excavators, apply to the New Zealand Customs Service for a client code, confirm the correct tariff classification of each excavator under the Working Tariff, and obtain import processing clearance before the first shipment. If the company is ultimately controlled by non-residents, assess whether the Overseas Investment Act 2003 applies to any asset purchase or business acquisition.
required_dossiers: Customs client code application and tariff classification
Beneficial ownership and overseas investment declaration if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD number or GST registration is delayed, call the Inland Revenue business helpline and provide proof of address and director identification; if customs classification is disputed, apply for a tariff classification ruling or binding determination from the New Zealand Customs Service.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open operational bank account and establish compliance file
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorised New Zealand bank or licensed trade finance bank, acting under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the operational bank account and complete customer due diligence. Provide the certificate of incorporation, constitution, list of directors, proof of ownership, and the first board resolution authorising the bank mandate. Because used heavy-machinery trading is classified by the bank as medium risk under its AML/CFT programme, each signatory may be required to attend in person or verify identity by video link, provide source of wealth or funds, and explain the projected transactions including wire transfers and Swift letters of credit. Maintain a compliance file containing the tax registration, customs client code, supplier and buyer due diligence, invoices, bills of lading, and the first board resolution. Confirm that no industrial manufacturing licence is required for wholesale remarketing; if the company later operates a depot, secure yard, or storage facility, obtain the territorial authority building occupancy approval, resource consent for any stormwater or noise effects, and fire safety certification.
required_dossiers: Director identification and bank account mandate
Customs client code and examples of invoices or bills of lading
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines or imposes enhanced due diligence, supply a board-approved source of wealth statement, detailed trade receipts, and a compliance narrative showing the legitimate origin and destination of each machine; if the decline persists, apply to a second-tier bank with trade finance expertise.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable for the registered trading scope of ISIC 4659; if a physical depot, workshop, or storage yard is later established, the competent authorities would be the territorial authority (city or district council), the regional council, and Fire and Emergency New Zealand.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial or physical operating licence is required by New Zealand law for wholesale remarketing and resale of secondhand hydraulic earthmovers and rollers. The activity does not fall under ISIC manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing codes requiring a separate operating permit.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable; the Ministry for the Environment and the relevant regional council would become the agencies only upon the addition of a depot, wash bay, maintenance workshop, or other physical activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt. The stated commercial activity triggers no environmental impact assessment, environmental registration, or resource consent category under the Resource Management Act 1991.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable. If future operations include cleaning, degreasing, or hydraulic fluid handling, the operator must comply with the Resource Management Act 1991, any regional plan discharge rules, and hazardous waste disposal requirements; used oil and contaminated water cannot be released to land or stormwater without an appropriate consent.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for an office-based trading operation. If a secure yard, showroom, or storage shed is used, the building must hold a building warrant of fitness or occupancy certificate under the Building Act 2004, and fire safety measures, means of egress, and emergency lighting must satisfy Fire and Emergency New Zealand requirements under the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017; heavy vehicle storage areas must also meet structural and load rating requirements.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Inland Revenue / Te Tari Taake) of New Zealand, operating through the myIR secure online portal and the New Zealand Customs Service for border controls.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A New Zealand-registered limited company obtains its IRD number automatically via the New Zealand Companies Office registration event; the company must then activate myIR and confirm its registration details. A non-resident foreign company deriving New Zealand-source income or making taxable supplies must apply for an IRD number and a GST registration through the Inland Revenue Department's myIR portal. The statutory application process requires the foreign entity to provide certified proof of incorporation, evidence of the registered office, the full legal name and physical residential address, identification of directors and ultimate shareholders, and the appointment of a New Zealand tax agent or authorised liaison if the company is not resident in New Zealand. If the non-resident is registering only for GST, the same myIR application process is used, and the IRD number serves as the combined tax and GST registration number. No entity-level TIN separate from the IRD number exists; the IRD number is the single national taxpayer identifier.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. New Zealand does not provide a check-the-box election similar to the United States. Cross-border hybrid mismatch adjustments are mandatory, not elective, under the Income Tax Act 2007 (subpart FH), and a company's tax classification follows its legal form under the Companies Act 1993.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance mandate exists in New Zealand. GST returns are filed electronically through myIR, and registered businesses must maintain and issue compliant tax invoices under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985. E-invoicing is voluntary and based on the PEPPOL interoperability framework; there is no anti-fraud digital stamping requirement.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A GST-registered exporter may claim the 0% (zero-rated) GST rate on supplies of used construction excavators and rollers under section 11 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 when the goods are exported from New Zealand by the supplier and leave New Zealand within 28 days of the time of supply. The supplier must obtain documentary proof of export, the goods must not be consumed in New Zealand, and the sale must be made to a non-resident purchaser or delivered to an overseas destination. Supplies of offshore services connected to the machinery trade may be zero-rated under section 11A where the services are supplied to a person not resident in New Zealand.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: New Zealand Customs Export Entry (CEE) lodged through the Trade Single Window
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export from New Zealand
Commercial invoice, packing list, and purchase contract
Inward foreign exchange repatriation evidence (bank credit advice, SWIFT MT103, or equivalent bank confirmation)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the exporter cannot substantiate that the goods were exported or that the sale proceeds were remitted to New Zealand within the required period, the supply is re-characterised as a standard-rated taxable supply at 15% GST, and Inland Revenue may issue a retroactive assessment, impose late payment interest, and apply civil penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994 and the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985. Deliberate false zero-rating claims, document fabrication, or unremitted foreign exchange with intent to evade GST may give rise to criminal prosecution, fines, and imprisonment. Exporters must retain the supporting export and foreign-exchange documentation for at least seven years for audit and verification.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains an open-market liberalised foreign exchange regime. The New Zealand dollar (NZD) is fully convertible, and no foreign exchange control regulations are in force to restrict current international transactions or outward capital transfers, provided settlements are conducted through registered banks and New Zealand tax filing/reporting obligations are met. New Zealand has accepted Article VIII of the IMF Articles of Agreement, entailing the absence of exchange controls or multiple currency practices. The principal gate is the Overseas Investment Act 2005; non-resident investment into a used-machinery trading company that does not touch sensitive land or exceed the current significant-business-assets threshold requires no Reserve Bank approval. Profit remittance is unrestricted from an exchange-control perspective: a New Zealand Ltd may pay dividends to a foreign shareholder after directors satisfy the Companies Act solvency test and Inland Revenue non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) is deducted where appropriate. There is no obligation to surrender export proceeds or to obtain permission for bank account funding, and no requirement that invoices be converted into NZD. The applicable checks are bank AML/CFT treatment, sanctions screening, and transfer-pricing substance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender rules apply in New Zealand. Mandatory conversion ratio is 0% and there is no legally specified timeline for converting export invoices into NZD. Exporters may hold foreign currency receipts in an onshore foreign-currency account or freely sell them to a registered bank at the prevailing market rate. For trade-based AML/CFT compliance, a bank may require the export invoice, proof of shipment (e.g., bills of lading or cargo manifests), and customs export entry before crediting proceeds, but this is documentary verification, not an exchange-control surrender. IRD reporting requirements (e.g., GST on exported second-hand goods, if applicable) continue to apply.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account (with Trade Finance/LC desk)
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account (with Trade Finance/LC desk)
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account (with Export/Import Settlement)
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account (with Documentary Collections)
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for ancillary cash management and inbound collections, Low as a sole treasury or capital-escrow rail. Foreign non-bank electronic money institutions (EMIs) such as offshore digital wallets and FX platforms are not registered banks in New Zealand and cannot provide deposit protection, formal Letters of Credit, bank guarantees, or trade loans under the Banking Prudential Supervision Act 1989. An offshore EMI is legally barred from servicing an NZ entity unless it is registered on the New Zealand Financial Service Providers Register (FSPR) for the relevant services and has an AML/CFT programme under the AML/CFT Act 2009. Even where such registration exists, an EMI cannot replace a Tier-1 bank for capital verification by an NZ auditor, settlement under a Commercial LC (UCP600), or documentary collections through a bank negotiator. The optimal blueprint uses a Tier-1 domestic bank for capital escrow and trade finance; an EMI may be used only for low-value supplier deposits or foreign-currency operating balances, with full reconciliation and sanctions screening maintained.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: New Zealand AML/CFT rules do not universally demand an in-branch appearance; identity may be verified using a 'safe and sound' process, including approved digital identity services (e.g., RealMe or NZ Post ID Verify) for local persons. However, for a Medium-Risk/Enhanced corporate entity trading used construction equipment with offshore ownership, major NZ banks generally require either a physical appointment for the statutory director(s) and beneficial owners or a live video/HO-certified interview through the bank's Non-Resident Banking desk. Remote consular proxy opening is not normally accepted as the primary KYC event because the bank must detect source-of-funds risk, politically exposed persons, and trade-based money-laundering indicators. In practice, a local director or a delegated officer with board authority must attend at least one video or in-branch meeting, with notarised corporate documents, passport certification, and a board resolution for account opening; some banks will accept a sworn affidavit verified by the overseas bank if the client relationship is already established.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex beneficial ownership chain involving offshore trusts, nominee shareholders, or opaque intermediate holding companies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate registers for every intermediate entity; percentages of ultimate beneficial ownership; a redacted trust deed showing discretionary beneficiaries and protectors; notarised source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements for each UBO; NZ Companies Office certificates of good standing; an organisational chart with share classes; and a written board-approved explanation of commercial rationale for the trust ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering red flag: under/over-invoicing or arbitrary pricing for used excavators with no independent valuation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent pre-shipment inspection reports (e.g., SGS, Bureau Veritas, or certified heavy-equipment surveyor); OEM serial-number/VIN and title/ownership history; auction or market-comparable appraisals from certified heavy-machinery valuers; original supplier invoices; certificates of origin; Bills of Lading with HS code 8429; destination-country customs entries; transport and logistics forwarding records for at least six months; and a documented pricing policy for expected trading margins.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound or outbound payments from high-risk or sanctioned jurisdictions, or remittances from third parties not party to the sales contract
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Real-time sanctions/PEP screening output for all transacting parties; six months of bank statements for the remitting entity; signed commercial contracts identifying the actual buyer and seller; export/import licences where required; tax invoices and customs declarations; evidence that the settlement account is owned by the contracted counterparty; insurance certificates covering the physical movement of the excavators; and a narrative explaining the trade flow and end-use.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient economic substance for a wholesale trading company, with projected turnover inconsistent with working capital or storage facilities
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Three-year business plan and cash-flow projections; warehouse or yard lease with proof of possession; purchase orders from both suppliers and end buyers; proposed stock list with historical auction pricing; staffing or outsourcing contracts; IRD registration confirmation; prior-year or forecast financial statements for the NZ entity; and evidence of equity or intercompany funding source, including loan agreements if relevant.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inward equity capital from the foreign parent should be wired as a SWIFT MT103 customer transfer to the NZ entity's capital escrow or equity subscription account at a Tier-1 registered bank. The remittance must state the purpose as 'DIRECT INVESTMENT - EQUITY CAPITAL' and include the invoice/reference number; New Zealand does not prescribe a national FX purpose-code list, but the bank will map the transfer under OECD Balance of Payments category 1.3 (Direct Investment Equity) for record-keeping. No Reserve Bank approval is required before receipt; however, if the NZ company will acquire sensitive land or significant business assets above the current Overseas Investment Act threshold, an OIO consent application must be filed before completion. Upon receipt, the bank will issue an inward foreign exchange settlement ticket if conversion to NZD is made; the shareholder resolution, subscription agreement, bank confirmation, inward remittance advice, and updated share register from the Companies Act allotment should be retained to prove capital verification. The funds must not be disbursed until the account is active and the bank confirms the source-of-funds review is complete.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For import-side settlements from New Zealand to overseas used-machinery vendors, the preferred rails are: (i) SWIFT MT103 for open-account payments or advance deposits against pro-forma invoices; (ii) Commercial Letters of Credit issued via MT700 under UCP600 for larger auctions or high-risk jurisdictions, with sight drafts and documents consisting of Bill of Lading, commercial invoice, packing list, and original OEM certificate; and (iii) Documentary Collections (DP/DA) using a bank transmission such as MT400 or MT410 when the buyer wants verification of documents without LC risk. For the export side from NZ to end buyers, receive funds by MT103; or ask the buyer's bank to open an LC in favour of the NZ entity, with the NZ exporting bank acting as confirming or negotiating bank. All outbound payments must embed invoice numbers and machine serial numbers in the remittance field, and the bank's Trade Finance desk should screen corresponding banks for OFAC and NZ sanctions compliance. NZD high-value settlements clear through RBNZ's Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS) with SWIFT message continuity, while USD/EUR/GBP settlements use the bank's foreign correspondent clearing network.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards in NZD/USD, NZD/AUD, NZD/EUR, and NZD/JPY for firm import/export exposures, executed under an ISDA 1998 FX Plus agreement or the bank's standard treasury terms, limited to underlying traded goods and with no leverage beyond the invoice value.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for emerging-market trade currencies that are not freely deliverable in New Zealand (e.g., IDR, VND, NGN), only where a genuine used-machinery purchase or sale is evidenced by a contract and the NDF notional equals the trade receivable or payable under the invoice.

FX swaps and cross-currency swaps to hedge working-capital mismatches between NZD operating funds and foreign-currency settlement accounts, approved by the board in a treasury policy that prohibits speculative uncovered positions.

European-style FX options (including zero-premium collars) for contingent tenders or auction bids where the quantity and price are not yet committed, provided the underlying trade documentation is maintained for the bank's periodic review.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return to the Companies Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies), Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the company's annual return date, being the registration anniversary as recorded on the Companies Register profile; the exact due date is stated in the Registrar's annual return reminder notice.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file by the due date exposes the company to a Notice of Intention to Remove; if the default is not remedied within 20 working days of that notice, the Registrar may strike the company off the New Zealand Register and gazette its dissolution. Restoration is discretionary, costly, and does not cure the period of administrative disability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For the standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 must be filed by 7 July following the tax year for e-filed returns, or by 7 May for paper returns. For non-standard balance dates, the statutory filing window is the 4th month after balance date for paper and the 6th month after balance date for electronic filing.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers late filing penalties and default assessments; unpaid tax attracts use-of-money interest plus a late payment penalty of 1% immediately, an additional 4% after 7 days, and 1% per month thereafter. Continued non-compliance may lead to IRD collection action, prosecution, and director liability in egregious cases.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: GST-registered traders must file at the prescribed frequency determined by turnover: monthly, two-monthly, or six-monthly in accordance with the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985; each return is due on the 28th day of the month following the close of the taxable period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing and non-payment expose the company to IRD late filing penalties, late payment penalties, use-of-money interest, default assessments, debt recovery proceedings, and potential strike-off action where revenue debts remain unsatisfied.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer Payday Filing / PAYE and Employer Annual Reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Where the NZ company employs staff, employment information must be filed every payday through the IRD payday filing system; if an annual employer reconciliation is still required by IRD after 31 March, it must be completed by 31 May following the tax year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Missing payday filings or annual reconciliations attract penalties, late payment interest, and criminal sanctions for deliberate tax evasion; IRD may recover unpaid PAYE from directors personally under the tax recovery provisions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: FBT returns are due quarterly on the 20th day of the month following the end of each quarter, namely 20 May, 20 August, 20 November, and 20 February for a standard 31 March balance date; an annual election return, where available, is due on 20 May following the tax year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts IRD penalties, use-of-money interest, and default assessments. Where fringe benefits are deliberately under-declared, substantial shortfall penalties and prosecution may follow.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Notification of Changes to Director, Registered Office, Address for Service, and Constitution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies), MBIE
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Not an annual obligation but a continuing maintenance filing: any change of directors, registered office, address for service, or other statutory particulars must be notified to the Registrar within 20 working days after the change occurs.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-notification is an offence under the Companies Act 1993 and results in inaccurate public records; the company may be flagged as non-compliant, annual returns may be rejected, and directors face monetary penalties on conviction.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Financial Statements and Annual Report (only where a statutory audit trigger is met)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies) and/or Financial Markets Authority (FMA) depending on FMC reporting status; otherwise, audited financial statements are delivered to shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For large or FMC reporting entities that are required to file, the audited financial statements and annual report must be lodged within 4 months after the balance date; for non-filing companies, audited financial statements must still be prepared and presented to shareholders within the statutory reporting period under the Financial Reporting Act 2013.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to prepare, audit, or file financial statements when required is an offence; penalties may be imposed on the company and each director, and the Registrar or FMA may issue compliance orders, while persistent default can support strike-off action.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Companies Act 1993 and Financial Reporting Act 2013, a mandatory independent audit by a licensed/certified CPA auditor applies where the company, including controlled subsidiaries, satisfies either (i) consolidated total assets exceeding NZD 60,000,000, or (ii) consolidated annual turnover exceeding NZD 30,000,000, in at least one of the two most recent consecutive accounting periods. An audit is also compulsory where the company is an FMC reporting entity, such as an issuer, registered bank, licensed insurer, or non-bank deposit taker, regardless of size. Employee headcount is not a statutory audit trigger under New Zealand law for an ordinary NZ limited company trading in used construction machinery; however, an audit may be contractually required by a financier, joint-venture agreement, or shareholder constitution and, if adopted, must comply with approved auditing standards.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must be prepared in accordance with accounting standards approved by the External Reporting Board (XRB) under the Financial Reporting Act 2013. Tier 1 for-profit entities apply NZ IFRS (New Zealand equivalents to IFRS); Tier 2 entities apply NZ IFRS with reduced disclosure; small non-publicly-accountable entities may apply simplified reporting frameworks permitted by the XRB. Entities that trigger the statutory audit threshold must present general-purpose financial statements in compliance with NZ IFRS unless an applicable exemption or reduced-disclosure regime is permitted by law.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not currently impose a separate annual UBO confirmation filing with the Companies Registrar. The NZ company must maintain an accurate private share register and directors' interests register, record every share transfer on the register as soon as it occurs, and reflect the resulting shareholder position in the next annual return. Changes of directors and registered office details must be filed with the Companies Office within 20 working days, not a 30-day window. To the extent the company is an AML/CFT obliged entity, beneficial owners must be identified, verified, and refreshed at least annually or whenever a material change in ownership occurs; the company must also make the necessary risk-based enhanced due diligence updates. For ordinary non-financial wholesale traders of used construction excavators, no standalone annual UBO filing to a government registry is presently required.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book containing shareholder and director resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$350 to US$1,200 per annum depending on provider, incorporation support, and corporate secretarial scope in New Zealand.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Where a full statutory audit is triggered, independent certified CPA audit fees typically range from US$25,000 to US$90,000 per annum depending on asset complexity, overseas related-party transactions, inventory valuation, and consolidation scope; small companies not requiring a statutory audit may incur US$4,000 to US$12,000 for an independent review or agreed-upon procedures if demanded by a lender or investor.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No free-zone tax holidays in New Zealand. Available credits include a 15% R&D tax incentive for eligible R&D expenditure; no patent box regime; loss carry-forward is conservatively benchmarked at 5 years for this structured filing, although New Zealand law applies shareholder continuity and business continuity tests in operation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR 4 Company Income Tax Return filed through the Inland Revenue myIR digital filing portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; provisional tax instalments are payable quarterly where total residual income tax exceeds NZD 5,000.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR 4 must be filed and terminal tax paid no later than 7 July, which is the 7th day of the fourth month after balance date; a tax agent extension may push filing obligations to a later date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total assessable income from wholesale trading of used construction excavators, rollers, and other hydraulic earthmovers, stated net of GST.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only New Zealand-source trading income. A non-resident company with no New Zealand permanent establishment should not file IR 4 unless New Zealand-source income is derived through a fixed place of business or dependent agent. If a PE exists, attribute income to that PE and attach a separate PE profit-attribution schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjustments to income and segregation of excluded non-resident source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use IFRS or NZ GAAP to apportion income between New Zealand and offshore activities. For used machinery sold FOB outside New Zealand with title passing offshore and no dependent agent in New Zealand, treat the gain as non-resident source income and attach bills of lading, shipping terms, and inspection certificates to support the exclusion.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All allowable business expenses, including cost of used excavator inventory, refurbishment, freight, insurance, customs duties, and brokerage.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Related-party service charges, management fees, and embedded royalties are allowed only when supported by a written agreement, evidence of actual service, arm's-length pricing, and the correct withholding tax treatment. Any royalty embedded in the purchase price of machinery must be separately identified and subject to non-resident withholding tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory add-backs and adjustments to expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back non-deductible entertainment costs, thin-capitalisation interest disallowance (New Zealand net debt exceeding 60% of net assets or group gross debt exceeding 110% of worldwide debt), transfer pricing adjustments arising from under-pricing to offshore affiliated traders, and non-deductible payments to foreign related parties that lack commercial substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income or loss before loss offsets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident company operating through a New Zealand branch, losses are ring-fenced and may be offset only against New Zealand source income. Do not absorb losses incurred by foreign sister companies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carry-forward utilised in the current year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a continuity schedule proving that at least 49% of shareholders and the same line of business have been maintained from the loss year to the current year. A change in non-resident ownership before the tax filing will invalidate the loss carry-forward.
This is the final base against which the 28% corporate income tax rate is applied. Do not net withholding tax credits or imputation credits against this field before calculation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Notional corporate income tax calculated at the statutory rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply 28% to the amount in Box 7. For a non-resident company with a New Zealand PE, only income attributable to the PE is taxable; the PE must provide a copy of the home-country tax treaty residency certificate where a DTA restriction applies.

Claim credits for New Zealand resident withholding tax on interest and dividends, and claim foreign tax credits only if a DTA supplies an applicable mechanism. Shareholder's imputation credits belong in the company's Imputation Credit Account; non-resident shareholders do not receive imputation credits through an offshore holding entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Residual income tax or refundable credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the taxpayer has overpaid provisional tax, ensure the refund is remitted only to a verified New Zealand or treaty-recipient bank account. For outbound dividends declared from the current year's profit, state the amount of imputation credits attached and the corresponding NRWT exposure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party transaction and transfer pricing declaration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory when aggregate cross-border related-party transactions exceed NZD 10 million. Attach a Master File and Local File, or a summary transfer pricing study, documenting the selected arm's-length methodology (CUP, resale price, cost plus, TNMM, or profit split), the benchmark comparables for wholesale used construction machinery, and the net margin achieved by the New Zealand entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Director's declaration and tax agent certification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A director of the New Zealand limited company must sign the declaration confirming that the return is true and correct and that all related-party transactions are at arm's length. Non-resident directors must supply an Inland Revenue file number and an address for service; failure to sign or omitting a deliberate false declaration may expose directors to personal liability.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the IR 4 invokes a NZD 250 late filing penalty per return. Late payment penalties for terminal tax are 1% immediately on the unpaid balance, with an additional 4% after seven days and a continuing monthly default component. Use-of-money interest accrues on unpaid tax daily. Knowingly filing a false return or evading assessment constitutes a criminal offence under section 144 of the Tax Administration Act 1994, exposing the company to fines up to NZD 50,000 and directors to imprisonment up to 10 years. Failure to maintain transfer pricing documentation when required can also trigger a documentation penalty of up to NZD 20,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Statutory Non-Resident Withholding Tax (NRWT) on outbound dividends is 30%; under most New Zealand double tax agreements the rate is reduced to 15%, and to 5% where the beneficial owner is a treaty-resident company holding at least 10% of the voting power in the New Zealand payer.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief on dividends, interest, or royalties, the non-resident recipient must provide the New Zealand payer with a valid Tax Residency Certificate issued by the competent authority of the treaty country, together with form IR290 or an equivalent rate-reduction certificate, and a signed beneficial-ownership declaration proving that the recipient is not a nominee or conduit. The payer must receive the certificate before payment to withhold at the treaty rate. If the certificate is not provided, the payer must withhold at the statutory NRWT rate; the recipient may then file a New Zealand tax return to claim a treaty refund and must be prepared to substantiate economic substance and the absence of back-to-back arrangements.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory NRWT on interest paid to non-residents is 15%, and the equivalent statutory rate on royalties is 15%. Under most New Zealand DTAs the rate on interest is reduced to 10%, and royalties are generally reduced to 10% or, in some protocols, 5%, depending on the type of intellectual property and the treaty partner. Interest that qualifies for the Approved Issuer Levy may be paid at a 2% levy only for approved public issuers, not for ordinary intercompany debt. All payments to related foreign persons must synchronise with arm's-length pricing and the Economic Substance / Core Income-Generating Activities analysis.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not maintain a separate Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) regime of the type imposed in zero-tax jurisdictions, but the Commissioner applies OECD-aligned transfer pricing rules and the general anti-avoidance provision in section BG 1 of the Income Tax Act 2007. Treaty benefits and PE profit attribution require the existence of substantial operational activity in New Zealand. Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) analysis is used to determine whether significant people functions exist in New Zealand for PE attribution, and thin-capitalisation rules restrict interest deductions for non-resident controlled entities. A company that cannot demonstrate commercial substance, real offices, actual trading risk, and substantive employees may be recharacterised as a sham or its financing deductions denied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and False Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately under-reporting New Zealand-source wholesale revenues, fabricating invoices for used excavator sales, recording the deal in an offshore sham entity while management decisions are made in New Zealand, and signing an IR 4 return that omits taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Prosecution under section 144 of the Tax Administration Act 1994: the company is liable to a fine of up to NZD 50,000 and the offending director to imprisonment for a term not exceeding 10 years; the Commissioner also imposes a 150% evasion shortfall penalty and recovers use-of-money interest on the unpaid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director who signs or causes the false return is personally jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax under section 165 of the Tax Administration Act 1994. Inland Revenue may issue a departure prohibition order for unpaid tax debt exceeding NZD 10,000, freezing the director's ability to leave New Zealand. The court may also confiscate the director's assets under the Criminal Proceeds (Recovery) Act 2009 and prohibit the director from managing a company under the Companies Act 1993.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling secondhand hydraulic earthmovers to a related Hong Kong or Singapore trading entity at a price far below arm's length, shifting profits outside New Zealand; the related entity then on-sells the machinery at a large margin to an end customer, while the New Zealand entity records a loss and continues to claim the 15% R&D credit for re-engineering support.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Commissioner adjusts the taxable income under sections GC 4 to GC 8 of the Income Tax Act 2007; the transfer pricing shortfall penalty is 20% for unsubstantiated documentation, escalating to 40% for gross carelessness and up to 150% for evasion. In addition, a NZD 20,000 penalty may be charged for failure to provide the mandatory transfer pricing documentation where cross-border related-party transactions exceed NZD 10 million.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who instructed or approved the artificial pricing and who fail to take reasonable steps to ensure accurate documentation are personally liable for the company's tax shortfall and the documentation penalty. New Zealand courts will pierce the corporate veil where the company is used as a façade for the directors' overseas asset shifting; directors face civil asset restitution, a departure prohibition order, disqualification from managing companies, and imprisonment if the manipulation is part of a wider fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Trade-Based Money Laundering and False Customs Declarations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the sale of used construction excavators as a conduit for money laundering through wire transfers and letters of credit, deliberately over-invoicing or under-invoicing machine values, altering serial numbers, erasing engine-hour records, and presenting forged certificates of origin to New Zealand customs and the foreign bank.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violation of the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 carries corporate penalties that can reach NZD 2 million for a reporting entity; customs offences under the Customs and Excise Act 2018 attract forfeiture of goods and vessels, fines, and, for serious fraud, imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior officers who knowingly participate in the money laundering scheme face criminal liability under the Crimes Act 1961 and the AML/CFT Act 2009. Personal civil liability includes restitution of laundered funds, asset freezing orders, seizure and forfeiture of personal property, mandatory blacklisting in the FIU watch-list, travel bans under the Tax Administration Act for unpaid tax, and imprisonment for up to 7 years where money laundering forms part of a major transaction.
